title: SPP3 EthID withdrawal — public-only retrospective reconstruction

selection.inclusionRationale: Selected after the first approved-award case because the public record contains an applicant withdrawal after committee selection but before final DAO cohort ratification. This directly stress-tests whether the v0.1 decision model can represent a real terminal lifecycle state without misclassifying it as approval, rejection, deferral, suspension, or pending.
selection.exclusionBoundary: This case reconstructs EthID's SPP3 selection-and-withdrawal lifecycle from public sources. It does not reconstruct the private application body, private individual scoring records, applicant-specific aggregate rubric scores, internal deliberations, or any later work outside the SPP3 candidacy.

initialFindings.rationale: The public record contains a terminal applicant withdrawal after committee selection and before final DAO ratification. v0.1 has no applicant-withdrawal lifecycle state. Substituting approved, rejected, deferred, suspended, or pending would materially misstate the observed process. This finding is evidence of a representational gap for this case, not a claim that every workflow requires a new institutional decision status.

The reviewed public artifacts establish that EthID passed the eligibility screen and was evaluated, but do not establish the exact eligibility-check timestamp required by schema v0.1. The null is retained instead of inventing a timestamp.

The reviewed public sources establish the authorization and rubric but this reconstruction does not have an exact source-supported effective timestamp for the combined governing policy represented here. The null is retained instead of fabricating one.

residualQuestions: Should a future schema represent applicant disposition or lifecycle events separately from institutional decision.status, so a withdrawal does not have to be forced into the institutional decision vocabulary?
If a future model adds applicant withdrawal, what authority and timestamp semantics should apply when the applicant acts after committee selection but before final DAO ratification?

What exact timestamp should a retrospective public-only record use for governingPolicy.effectiveAt when the source set combines an authorization and a later published rubric without a single machine-readable policy-version activation event?
When exactly was EthID's eligibility screen completed? Public evidence establishes qualification and selection but not the required checkedAt instant.
What were EthID's aggregate rubric scores? The committee states applicants may request their own aggregated scores privately, but reviewed public sources do not publish EthID's scores.
Were any conflicts or substantive disagreements recorded for EthID in internal committee working documents? The public record does not establish them.

The May 14 timeline lists submissions closing June 9, while the later cohort narrative states submissions closed June 4. The case preserves the discrepancy rather than choosing one without further evidence.
Because structural schema findings short-circuit semantic conformance, absence of semantic findings in this case is not evidence that all v0.1 semantic obligations were satisfied.

nonClaims: This corpus case does not reassess applicant merit.
Missing public evidence does not prove a private or internal procedure did not exist.
Validator success does not establish substantive correctness, fairness, or institutional legitimacy.
The $1,200,000 figure is a recommended-cohort amount removed after withdrawal; it is not represented as a final award, payment, or receipt.

Classifying the withdrawal-status finding as a model defect is a case-specific representational conclusion, not a claim that the v0.1 institutional decision-status vocabulary should simply be expanded with an applicant lifecycle state.
Reference-only source URIs in this case are not represented as exact byte-preserved captures.
